summary: Transient latency spike on api-gateway /api/v1/users endpoint. P99 latency spiked from a baseline of ~130ms to a peak of 3100ms between 14:30-14:50 UTC, exceeding the 1s SLO threshold for 4 consecutive intervals. Latency has since recovered to baseline.
root_cause: Upstream dependency degradation (likely database) caused request queuing and increased response times. The spike pattern (gradual increase → peak → recovery) is consistent with a transient backend resource constraint that self-resolved.
evidence: Spike onset at 14:30 UTC: latency jumped from 120ms to 450ms (3.75x increase)
SLO threshold (1s) exceeded for 4 intervals: 14:35-14:50 UTC
Recovery observed at 14:55 UTC: latency dropped to 180ms
Full recovery by 15:00 UTC: latency returned to 130-140ms baseline
recommendations: Correlate with database metrics — check postgres query latency during 14:30-14:50 window
Review connection pool metrics for exhaustion events in the same timeframe
Set up SLO-based alerting: alert if p99 > 1s for more than 3 consecutive intervals
Consider implementing request timeout at 2s to prevent cascading slowdowns
Add client-side retry with exponential backoff for transient failures
anomalies_detected: Latency spike from 120ms to 3100ms (25.8x) between 14:30-14:45 UTC
4 consecutive SLO threshold violations (> 1s) indicating sustained degradation
Rapid recovery pattern suggests transient issue rather than permanent degradation
